newsitem.title: USA: Palmdale, Lancaster, Calif., consider tax merger.
newsitem.headline: Palmdale, Lancaster, Calif., consider tax merger.

text.p: The California cities of Palmdale and Lancaster are considering an unprecedented plan to pool their future sales tax revenues, according to a published report on Monday.
The exact terms of the agreement have yet to be worked out, The Los Angeles Times reported.
The plan, which may require voter approval, calls for Palmdale and Lancaster to split all of their revenues evenly, based on population, the Times said.
The cities would, in turn, stop battling each other for retailers, a costly practice of offering tax breaks, loans and other incentives to lure major businesses.

"We could be using the money we offer to retailers (for) parks, libraries, hiking trails, public safety," Palmdale City Manager Bob Toone told the Times. "We can start operating like cities instead of real estate dealers."
The Palmdale-Lancaster tax sharing proposal will be discussed at an August 18 meeting of the Antelope Valley Regional Partnership, which is chaired by both cities' mayors.
